parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized that Atlas had to be reimplemented from observed CLI behavior only and chose a Python stdlib strategy with SQLite support.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It assigned 13 children to probe command areas and write spec files, then after the swarm returned launched one coder child for the core CLI skeleton.
parallel.implementation: Most completed parallel work was behavioral documentation under /workspace/specs; the implementation child began reading specs and probing framework details but did not finish a working executable.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contained spec files, assets, an existing executable, and no demonstrably integrated from-scratch replacement accepted by artifact validation.
parallel.verification: The exploration children ran many command probes and some local comparisons, but no integrated final reimplementation test completed after the implementation child was launched.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The only implementation child was stopped before finishing; status.json records artifact validation ok false and the official evaluator compile_failed with no tests run.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same observation-only Atlas reimplementation task and the broad command surface implied by the bundled assets and help text.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept ownership in the main trajectory without delegation, iteratively probing behavior and writing implementation files directly in src.
serial.implementation: It produced a Go implementation skeleton with CLI/help behavior, HCL lexer and formatter files, utilities, stubs, helptext, and tests/ref material.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact included concrete source files and generated helptext/reference material, but the build did not pass before timeout.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran local diffs showing help outputs and some error paths matched the reference, then ran go vet/go build checks that exposed a compile issue.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run ended with vet reporting a compile error in src/hcl/format.go and was cancelled before fixing it; official evaluation also reports compile_failed and no tests run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the cleanroom reverse-engineering rules and the Atlas CLI breadth, then documented behavior across command areas.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same cleanroom task and worked from the same prompt and asset set while directly implementing observed behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-level outcome difference was proven; parallel converted requirements into broad spec gathering first, while serial immediately combined probing with implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the task into 13 probe scopes and deferred build ownership to a later single coder child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation or subagents and kept the implementation path in one main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel allocated early capacity to independent investigation, whereas serial kept probing, coding, and fixing under one owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received 13 dense spec handoffs and then described a module architecture for a Python zipapp before briefing a coder child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained the accumulated context locally while writing Go modules and did not need cross-agent interface handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced an explicit parent-to-child handoff after a bulk research phase; serial avoided that boundary but still made ordinary coding mistakes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel planned a Python stdlib zipapp, but the actual late coder child remained unfinished at cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a Go codebase with files such as hcl/format.go and validated parts of CLI help output before hitting a compile defect.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial produced more concrete source implementation, while parallel mostly delivered specs and an incomplete implementation handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The research swarm returned completed summaries, but the subsequent implementation child was still active when the parent turn was cancelled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main loop also timed out, but there was no child result lifecycle to join or recover from.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a late delegated implementation result that never became available; serial's unfinished state was a local compile-fix interruption.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children shared /tmp/probe and one child observed that another actor had overwritten its SQLite probe database; a second saw stale bad.hcl in the same area.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial validation reported no delegation or subagents, so there was no cross-agent scratch-space collision channel.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had observable shared-environment contamination among concurrent probes; serial's single trajectory avoided this coordination-specific shared-state hazard.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified many individual probe outputs and one completion-script comparison, but never completed whole-implementation acceptance after the implementation child started.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran direct local comparisons that matched several help/error paths, then go vet exposed a compile error before final acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked successful final acceptance; parallel's missing acceptance followed an uncompleted delegated build, while serial's missing acceptance followed a local compile error.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after a high-token, 14-subagent run with the implementation child still unfinished.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but under a no-delegation control after spending its budget in one implementation trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The budget failure was common to both official outcomes, but parallel's budget was consumed by an explore-first parallel plan before implementation closure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both completed evaluations failed with compile_failed and 0/1732 tests run. The parallel run's coordination left it with a cancelled late implementation child and an artifact dominated by specs, while the serial run produced more source code but ended with a local Go compile/vet error.
parallel_contributors: Explore-first pseudo-concurrency deferred productive implementation until after 13 child probes returned.
The active implementation child was cancelled before producing a complete replacement executable.
Shared /tmp/probe contamination invalidated at least one child probe and caused avoidable rework.
serial_contributors: Serial made direct source-code progress under one owner and verified some help paths.
Serial still failed because a compile/vet error in src/hcl/format.go remained unfixed at timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's final failure was an ordinary code defect in the Go HCL formatter rather than a concurrency boundary.
Parallel's final artifact did not show a completed integrated Python implementation before cancellation.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No official outcome difference; retained labels describe realized adverse parallel-side process consequences only.

candidates.reason: Parallel did assign implementation ownership: the parent first held the architecture plan and then launched a core CLI skeleton coder, so implementation was late and unfinished rather than ownerless.
No set of independently implemented components reached a state requiring cross-agent integration; the child implementation never completed.
The artifact was incomplete, but the parent had planned final zipapp/build placement; the observed failure was that implementation never finished, not that assembly ownership was omitted.
The parent explicitly owned the end-to-end transition from probing to architecture to implementation; it failed by sequencing and timeout, not by leaving the pipeline unowned.
There was no single mandatory preflight or oracle gate; the gating event was a broad first phase of many completed investigations.

The parent ran a 13-child investigation swarm as a separate first phase, consumed the returned specs, and only then launched one implementation child, which was stopped before producing a deliverable.
candidates.realized_consequence: The build phase was deadline-constrained and the only implementation child was cancelled before delivering the executable.
candidates.near_match_reason: Fan-out breadth contributed, but the most specific observed boundary was the completed investigation phase gating all productive implementation.

candidates.reason: The indispensable path did start late, but that is already captured as Serial Investigation; there is no separate allocation episode with distinct anchors and consequence.
The 13-child fan-out is real, but all research children returned and the direct retained boundary is implementation deferred behind that research phase rather than fan-out alone.
The late coder brief was broad, but the evidence does not isolate overbroad child scope as distinct from the preceding serial investigation and cancellation chain.
The child briefs included task scope, cleanroom rules, probing method, deliverable paths, and acceptance-like detail; no known requirement omitted from a child brief was shown to make work unusable.
The completed first-wave outputs were markdown specifications, not separately owned interoperating implementation components with incompatible contracts.
No known finding is shown present before transfer and missing after transfer; the parent summarized and used the returned spec set.
The 13 reports were large, but the parent explicitly reduced them into an architecture plan and launched implementation; the uncompleted build is better explained by serial investigation timing.
No parent or child is shown consuming a superseded handoff as the basis for implementation; the stale artifacts were shared scratch files, handled as contamination instead.
The record does not show incompatible child reports reaching the parent and remaining unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parent did not make an observable whole-task completion decision; the run was cancelled with an unfinished coder child and then failed artifact/evaluator checks.
There was no replacement child or retry that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints; the late coder was a first implementation assignment.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The implementation child was stopped at run cancellation, but retaining it would double-count the same chain already captured by Serial Investigation, whose correction would have started build work earlier.
No complete directly promotable implementation candidate or compatible component set existed before closure; the coder child was still unfinished.
No implementation result was merged after integrated verification; the implementation child did not complete a result to merge.
The delegated implementation was not completed or retrievable; missing join requires completed implementation work that the parent failed to adopt.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that failed to return to the parent before closure.
The cancelled implementation child was a terminal symptom of the same explore-first timing chain; no separate post-failure takeover window is evidenced.
The completed research results were returned and used in the parent's implementation plan; no concrete completed child result was ignored.
The parent was not merely waiting blindly on available results; it had inspected the completed research handoff and launched the implementation child before cancellation.
The research children wrote separate spec files; no competing implementation files or overlapping build ownership required cross-file reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown editing the same final source or configuration file with one observing or reconciling the other's concurrent change.
The overwritten object was a temporary probe database, not non-entry source produced or owned by another implementation agent.
No required executable or submitted entry-point source is shown being overwritten by a concurrent actor.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced another agent's final-tree implementation outputs.
The concrete proven problem is contaminated temporary probe input rather than unstable final implementation workspace writes.
Concurrent probe agents used a shared /tmp/probe area; one child observed its database had been overwritten by another actor and another found stale bad.hcl state, contaminating probe inputs.
candidates.realized_consequence: A probe observation was invalidated and had to be rerun in a private scratch directory, adding rework and leaving a caution about contaminated early outputs.
candidates.near_match_reason: The direct harm was polluted temporary artifacts consumed during probing, not a final workspace write collision or source/deliverable overwrite.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel run completed a large investigation-only swarm before starting productive implementation, leaving the implementation child to be cancelled before delivering a finished executable.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Productive implementation was left unfinished when the late implementation child was cancelled.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Fan-out and budget pressure were present, but the qualifying mistake was the serial investigation gate that delayed implementation until after the research phase.

retained_patterns.reason: Shared /tmp/probe artifacts from concurrent children polluted another child's behavioral probes, including an overwritten database and stale HCL file observations.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The affected child discarded the polluted result path and repeated key probes in a private directory.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The observed episode concerned leaked scratch artifacts contaminating probes, not concurrent final-source or final-workspace writes.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, Critical-Path Starvation, Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Oversized Child Task, and Blind Timeout Wait were not separately retained for the same explore-first-to-cancelled-child chain.
Unisolated Workspace Writes, Same-File Collision, and overwrite labels were not retained for the shared /tmp/probe episode because Artifact Leakage is the more specific contamination boundary.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; retained patterns are limited to directly evidenced realized coordination harm.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No timeout, child-count, stale-todo, or ordinary compile-defect symptom was promoted into a separate label without a distinct episode and consequence.
